evidence.detail: 2026-10-11: FileNotFoundError: local/Version.txt; ERROR: Failed to build ... when getting requirements to build wheel

claim: At revision 43cef367cd0b2cf00cc03064ca9d29d1ff507967, setup.py and package.py read local/Version.txt, the directory local/ is git-ignored and untracked, and pip install . fails with FileNotFoundError on a fresh clone.
suggested_issue_title: Aspose.Page FOSS for Python: pip install . fails on a fresh clone because local/Version.txt is not in the repository
suggested_issue_body:
## Summary

Installing the package from a fresh clone fails. `setup.py` (line 35) reads the package version from `local/Version.txt`, and `package.py` (line 45) reads the same file, but `.gitignore` (line 9) excludes the whole `local/` directory, so the file is not in the repository. The README documents the source build (`python package.py build`) and says the wheel version comes from `local/Version.txt` (README.md lines 98 and 102).

## Environment

- Repository: aspose-page-foss/Aspose.Page-FOSS-for-Python
- Revision: `43cef367cd0b2cf00cc03064ca9d29d1ff507967` (the upstream revision this report was verified against, default branch `main`)
- Windows 11, Python 3.13.15, pip 26.2.1
- Verified on 2026-10-11 from a fresh shallow clone.

## Steps to reproduce

```
git clone https://github.com/aspose-page-foss/Aspose.Page-FOSS-for-Python
cd Aspose.Page-FOSS-for-Python
git ls-files local | wc -l
pip install . --no-deps
```

## Expected

`pip install .` builds and installs the package from a clean clone, or the documentation says how to create `local/Version.txt` first.

## Actual

`git ls-files local | wc -l` prints `0`, and the install stops while preparing the wheel:

```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../local/Version.txt'
ERROR: Failed to build 'file:///.../Aspose.Page-FOSS-for-Python' when getting requirements to build wheel
```

## Where in the repository

- `setup.py:35` and `package.py:45` (both read `local/Version.txt`)
- `.gitignore:9` (`local/`)
- `README.md:98` and `README.md:102`

## Suggested fix

Track a default `local/Version.txt` (and ignore only the credential files kept in `local/`), or fall back to the `version` declared in `pyproject.toml` when the file is missing.
